content:
Hi all, this is my first Zulip post. I am curious on any techniques anyone knows for optimizing (specifically wrt rebuild times) and mechanizing a deep embedding of a DTT in Lean 4:

  1. My (local) confluence proof is extremely long. Occasionally, I will have to make slight changes to my reduction rules. This will require several hours of updating my confluence proof. Is there any literature you all can point me to on mechanizing confluence or any techniques to speed this up?
  2. My project structure is quite linear. This means if I make a slight change to my AST, my type-checker will take on average 5-7 minutes to rebuild. Are there any lake flags I can use to help with this? I am considering using Lean modules, since I have not adopted them yet. I have noticed that Lean never maxes out my RAM or CPU. I have 16 cores and 64 GB of RAM, so it seems like something is wrong there.
  3. What is the general strategy for organizing aesop and grind theorems for DTT metatheory? I have custom aesop sets, but I would like to know practically what the best way to group them is. Right now I have them organized with a priority ("heavier" aesop sets) and by which part of the metatheory they are for (e.g., reduction, inference, judgments, term sizes, etc.). I suspect grind is where the bottleneck is happening with my build times.
  4. General type theory question: my reduction relation has global confluence, but the paths are not deterministic, since I use call by value operational semantics. Hence, Red lives in Prop. Is there an established way to have deterministic reduction paths and CBV? I have hand-rolled my own before but I would like to know if there is a well-known approach already before I re-roll it.

Most of the type theory literature is on Agda and Rocq, so I am asking the Zulip. Some background on my setup: it is a deep embedding of a combinatory type theory, so there are many constructors for single-step reduction, many constructors for the AST, and many for judgments. I also have strong normalization by a size measure, so I would like to avoid parallel reduction, since it is not necessary. I would also ideally like to avoid normalization by evaluation. I am curious if anyone has had any success with abstracting their reduction relation with some existing term rewriting system (e.g., if there is any machinery in CSLib).

Thanks very much!
